propositions: Packaged prose guides cite criterion ids inline without coupling to the criteria registry, allowing a criterion's rubric to be rewritten silently while guide claims about it become false.
When criterion text changes, there is no mechanism to detect that a guide's paraphrase of it is now inaccurate, as demonstrated by bug 828a which drifted undetected for a month.
A citation pin manifest derived from the criteria registry can make criterion text changes visible by failing a gate when a criterion's digest no longer matches its pin, forcing re-verification.

The pin gate must extract citations from guides using vocabulary-only matching against CANONICAL_LLM at word boundaries, independent of prose markup or structure, so ordinary guide edits do not break the gate.
The gate must report four failure classes: unknown citation (criterion removed/renamed), stale pin (criterion text changed), orphan pin (criterion no longer cited), and missing manifest.
Regenerated pins must be packaged with guides, run in CI without new steps by composing into validate-routing, and be idempotent and byte-canonical.
